argument: Within hierarchical part-instance segmentation over point clouds using a maximal part-tree template, mask-sum constraint M_j = sum of child masks M_k for each parent j is associated with consistency between predicted part masks and the part-tree template hierarchy under the constraint ensures children masks sum exactly to the parent mask, with the root mask fixed to one.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported hierarchical segmentation adaptation and its part-tree template construction; other hierarchical output structures are unestablished.
claim: In hierarchical part-instance segmentation, enforcing that each parent part mask equals the sum of its child part masks, implemented by a SoftMax operation over the children masks, maintains consistency with a predefined part-tree template.
conditions: a maximal instance-level part-tree template is defined from training data
the number of output masks matches the number of template nodes
a SoftMax operation is applied over all children masks for each parent
falsifier: Implement the mask-sum constraint in a hierarchical segmentation model and verify that predicted parent masks equal the sum of their child masks across a held-out set of part-tree templates.
interpretation: The evidence supports a formal proposition concerning hierarchical part-instance segmentation over point clouds using a maximal part-tree template.
